9-panel cinematic storyboard CONTACT SHEET derived from Image 1. Mix Wide, Medium, and Tight shots of the same scene.

Layout: a rigid 3x3 grid of 9 equal rectangular cells in a 16:9 landscape image. Each cell is exactly 1/3 of the width and 1/3 of the height. Separate cells with a thin black gutter.
- Content must not cross, bleed, or overlap a gutter. No collage.
- Each cell is a complete, independently framed shot — not a crop of a larger scene.

Scene: medium wide, eye level, Scarlett (Image 2) has just stepped into the crowded crosswalk, filming herself with one hand while keeping her coffee level with the other, Scarlett (Image 2) moves through the crosswalk on the center third, taxis and office towers layered behind her, phone raised and coffee held in the foreground, EXT. DOWNTOWN CROSSWALK — LATE MORNING, late morning, downtown_crosswalk (Image 3), Bright late-morning daylight reflects sharply from office glass and vehicle surfaces. Wind and changing light keep the scene visually active as the crowd passes., Concrete gray, taxi colors, reflective blue-gray glass, black and charcoal clothing, warm skin tones, and small coral accents., Modern social-first product photography with tactile, editorial energy. Products shown in real-life context -- hands opening packaging, fingers pressing textures, products on bathroom shelves, kitchen counters, rumpled linen. Close-up detail shots emphasize material and finish. Flat-lays with curated minimal arrangements. Color-matched backgrounds that complement the product. Every frame feels like something you would screenshot and save

Every panel is a shot of the same scene as Image 1 — keep the characters, wardrobe, lighting, color grade, and texture consistent across all panels.

No text, dialogue bubbles, scene numbers, or watermarks.

Reference images define identity — keep every referenced character, object, and location consistent with its reference image; never render a reference image itself as a separate panel or subject.
Image 1 (primary): Primary source scene — generate 9 variant shots from this image
